title: Suffixes: forming adjectives
subtitle: comfortable, musical, useful, careless
summary: Make adjectives from nouns and verbs with -al, -able, -ful and -less, and form their opposites with un- and -less.

lesson.heading: Adjective suffixes
lesson.text: Common endings that make adjectives are **-able** (comfortable), **-al** (musical), **-y** (cloudy), **-ous** (famous) and **-ive** (attractive). If you know the suffix, you can often guess the adjective from a noun or a verb.

lesson.heading: -al
lesson.text: Adjectives ending in **-al** are usually formed from nouns, and they often mean 'relating to that noun'.

lesson.heading: -al adjectives in a text
lesson.text: Shichi-Go-San (meaning 7, 5, 3) is an **annual** ceremony in Japan for young girls and boys. It is on 15 November, but it is not a **national** holiday - a holiday for the whole country - so families often celebrate it at the weekend. Odd numbers have **cultural** significance in Japan, because they are lucky. On that day children may wear **traditional** clothes, in a style that has continued for hundreds of years, although today it is quite **normal** for them to wear western-style clothes.

examples.text: The festival is an **annual** event, held on the first Monday in September.
Children perform **traditional** dances at the ceremony.

lesson.heading: -able and its opposite with un-
rows: pleasant to sit or lie in
able to be trusted or believed
fair; not a bad decision or price
lesson.note: The suffix -able forms adjectives from nouns and verbs, and the prefix un- usually forms the opposite.

lesson.heading: When the un- form is the common one
lesson.text: Sometimes the negative adjective is the one people use most.

examples.text: She told us an **unbelievable** story about a dog that could speak.
examples.note: very surprising and hard to believe

lesson.heading: -ful and -less
rows: with a lot of colour in it
lesson.note: -ful means 'full of' or 'having the quality of the noun'. Only some of these words make their opposite with -less: we say useless and careless, but not wonderless or peaceless.

lesson.text: The suffix is -ful with one l, so write useful and careful, not ~~usefull~~ or ~~carefull~~.

exercises.prompt: You must be very ___ when you drive in wet weather.
The tourist information office was very ___, and told us everything we needed to know.
exercises.explanation: A helpful person or office gives a lot of help.

exercises.prompt: Match each adjective with the noun it usually goes with.
Which suffix makes an adjective from each noun?
She told us an ___ story about a dog that could speak.
exercises.explanation: Something very surprising and hard to believe is unbelievable.

exercises.prompt: The festival is an ___ event, held on the first Monday in September.
exercises.explanation: An annual event happens once a year.

exercises.prompt: It was very ___ when I hit my leg against the corner of that table.
exercises.explanation: pain + -ful = painful. The opposite is painless.

exercises.prompt: This bag is ___; it's too small for me to put anything in it.
exercises.explanation: The opposite of useful is useless.

exercises.prompt: We've never had any problems with our TV in ten years; it's been very ___.
exercises.explanation: Something reliable can be trusted to work well.

exercises.prompt: Which of these -ful adjectives make an opposite with -less?
This is just my ___ opinion; others may not agree.
exercises.explanation: A personal opinion is the opinion of one person.

exercises.statement: Travelling round China and the Far East was an unforgetable experience.
exercises.explanation: Travelling round China and the Far East was an unforgettable experience. Forget doubles its final t before -able.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order to ask about a dress for a wedding.
exercises.answer: Do you think this dress is suitable for a wedding?
exercises.explanation: Suitable means right or correct for a particular situation.
